questions.question: How many bones does an adult human have?
questions.fun_fact: Babies are born with about 300 bones, many of which fuse together over time.

questions.question: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.fun_fact: Two hearts pump blood to the gills, the third serves the rest of the body.

questions.question: How many keys does a classic piano have?
questions.fun_fact: 52 white and 36 black keys make 88 in total.

questions.question: How many seconds are there in a day?
questions.fun_fact: 24 hours x 60 minutes x 60 seconds = 86,400 seconds.

questions.question: How tall is the Eiffel Tower in metres?
questions.fun_fact: Including antennas it stands about 330 metres tall today; originally 300.

questions.question: How many countries are there on the African continent?
questions.fun_fact: With 54 recognised states, Africa has the most countries of any continent.

questions.question: How many teeth does an adult dog have?
questions.fun_fact: Dogs have ten more teeth than humans, who have 32.

questions.question: In which year was the first email sent?
questions.fun_fact: Ray Tomlinson sent the first email over ARPANET in 1971.

questions.question: How many colours does a rainbow traditionally have?
questions.fun_fact: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

questions.question: How many pieces are on a chessboard at the start of a game?
questions.fun_fact: 16 pieces per player, 32 in total.

questions.question: Roughly how many litres of blood does an adult human have?
questions.fun_fact: About 5 litres, around 7 to 8 percent of body weight.

questions.question: How many crewed Moon landings have there been?
questions.fun_fact: Six Apollo missions landed successfully between 1969 and 1972.

questions.question: How many players per team are on the pitch in football (soccer)?
questions.fun_fact: Ten outfield players plus one goalkeeper.

questions.question: On average, how many days does a human pregnancy last?
questions.fun_fact: About 40 weeks, roughly 280 days from the last cycle.

questions.question: How many strings does a standard guitar have?
questions.fun_fact: A standard guitar has six strings, tuned E-A-D-G-B-E.

questions.question: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.fun_fact: Insects have six legs, which is why spiders are arachnids rather than insects.

questions.question: How many days are there in a leap year?
questions.fun_fact: Century years only count as leap years when divisible by 400, so 2000 was one and 1900 was not.

questions.question: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
questions.fun_fact: Pierre de Coubertin picked colours that, together with the white background, covered every national flag of his day.

questions.question: How many squares are there on a chessboard?
questions.fun_fact: In the old wheat legend, doubling the grains on each square adds up to more than 18 quintillion grains.

questions.question: How many hours are there in a week?
questions.fun_fact: Sleep eight hours a night and 56 of them are spent in bed.

questions.question: How many teeth does an adult have, wisdom teeth included?
questions.fun_fact: Children manage with 20 milk teeth, and plenty of adults never grow some or all of their wisdom teeth.

questions.question: How tall is the Statue of Liberty from the ground to the tip of the torch, in metres?
questions.fun_fact: The copper figure itself is about 46 metres; the rest is pedestal and foundation.

questions.question: In which year did the Titanic sink?
questions.fun_fact: She went down on the night of 14 to 15 April, on her maiden voyage.

questions.question: How many metres per second does sound travel through air at 20 °C?
questions.fun_fact: That is why every three seconds between lightning and thunder put the storm roughly one kilometre away.

questions.question: How tall is the Empire State Building up to its roof?
questions.fun_fact: With its antenna it reaches 443 metres, and the whole tower went up in about 13 months.

questions.question: How many legs does a lobster have, counting the ones with claws?
questions.fun_fact: That makes it a decapod, literally 'ten-footed', with the big claws on the front pair.

questions.question: In which year did Columbus's ships first reach the Americas?
questions.fun_fact: He landed on an island in the Bahamas on 12 October and died believing he had reached Asia.

questions.question: How many stars are on the flag of Europe?
questions.fun_fact: The number stands for perfection and has nothing to do with how many countries belong to the EU.

questions.question: How many cards are in a standard deck without jokers?
questions.fun_fact: Add up every card value from ace (1) to king (13) across all four suits and you get 364.

questions.question: How many coloured stickers does a classic Rubik's Cube have?
questions.fun_fact: The cube can be scrambled into more than 43 quintillion different positions.

questions.question: At how many degrees Fahrenheit does water boil at sea level?
questions.fun_fact: On the same scale water freezes at 32 degrees.

questions.question: How many pips are there on a standard die in total?
questions.fun_fact: Opposite faces of a standard die always add up to seven.

questions.question: How many neck vertebrae does a giraffe have?
questions.fun_fact: Exactly as many as a human — a giraffe's are just around 25 centimetres long each.

questions.question: In which year were the first modern Olympic Games held?
questions.fun_fact: Winners in Athens received a silver medal and an olive branch, not gold.

questions.question: How tall is the Burj Khalifa in Dubai?
questions.fun_fact: It was called Burj Dubai until its opening in 2010, when it was renamed after the UAE's president.

questions.question: How many ribs does a human have?
questions.fun_fact: The bottom two pairs are called floating ribs because they are not attached to the breastbone at the front.

questions.question: How many Earth days does a year on Mars last?
questions.fun_fact: A Martian day, at a little over 24 hours and 39 minutes, is barely longer than ours.

questions.question: What is the average distance between the Earth and the Moon?
questions.fun_fact: The Moon drifts about 3.8 centimetres further away from us every year.

questions.question: How long is the Golden Gate Bridge's main span between its two towers?
questions.fun_fact: When it opened in 1937 it was the longest suspension bridge span in the world.

questions.question: How many Earth days does Mercury take to orbit the Sun once?
questions.fun_fact: Yet one sunrise-to-sunrise day there lasts about 176 Earth days, two whole Mercury years.
